View all A new Nissan Skyline is slated for release around 2027, featuring retro-styled design cues, a 3.0L twin-turbo V6 engine, and a potential manual transmission option. This performance-oriented sedan, teased in Japan, is expected to come to the U.S. as a new Infiniti sport sedan, effectively acting as a successor to the Infiniti Q50. Key Details on the New Nissan Skyline/Infiniti (2026-2027) Design & Performance: The upcoming model is designed to blend heritage styling from the 1960s with modern performance, aiming to sit between the Nissan Z and GT-R in terms of lineup positioning. Engine & Specs: Reports suggest a 3.0-liter V6 twin-turbo engine producing roughly 450 horsepower. Transmission: A manual transmission option is highly anticipated. U.S. Market: The vehicle is expected to arrive in the United States as an Infiniti-badged sedan, continuing the long-standing trend of rebranding the Japanese-market Nissan Skyline for American luxury consumers. Context: While the current Skyline (V37) has been sold as the Infiniti Q50 in the U.S., the new generation aims to revive interest in the brand with a focus on driving dynamics. Historical Relationship Infiniti G35/G37: Beginning in 2002, the Skyline was exported to North America as the Infiniti G35 and later the G37. Infiniti Q50/Q60: The 13th-generation Skyline was sold in the U.S. as the Infiniti Q50 sedan, with the Q60 as the coupe variant. Shared Identity: The Skyline has always functioned as a bridge between luxury and performance for Nissan. Note: The information above is based on announcements and developments as of April 2026.
